correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the exact k>=2, R>0 claim from the frozen seven-file Git record and verified its tree hash independently using the seven actual blob IDs (0a861942a66fcd342985df796b9d62efa1d3d9bb). The convex hull equals K={(x,y):x^2+g_Q(y)^2<=R^2}: the gauge set is convex and contains all disks; conversely every fixed-x section sqrt(R^2-x^2)Q is a convex combination of the original disks at that SAME x. Fubini gives V=(4R^3/3) Area(Q); the 2k cyclic vertices +/-u_j imply Area(Q)=sum_j sin(delta_j). For each polygon edge subtending gamma in (0,pi), the ruled patch F(x,t)=(x,sqrt(1-x^2)[(1-t)u+tv]) has |F_x cross F_t|=2sin(gamma/2)sqrt(1-x^2sin^2(gamma/2)), independent of t. Integrating in x produces gamma+sin(gamma); summing the 2k edges (total gamma=2pi) gives S=2pi R^2+2R^2 sum sin(delta_j), hence S=2pi R^2+(3/(2R))V. Seams and endpoint tips have zero 2D area; no planar facets occur for positive gaps. Strict concavity of sin on (0,pi) gives the all-k equal-gap equality case, and the boundary vector (epsilon,...,epsilon,pi-(k-1)epsilon) gives strict unattained infima. Regular 2k-gon inradius tends R as k grows, giving Hausdorff ball convergence; both metric limits follow. Independent Python/SciPy calculations reconstructed the actual hull from 512 sampled points per source circle for random k=2,3,5, radius R=1.3, with relative volume errors <4e-5 and surface errors <2.4e-5; separate cross-product quadrature at gamma=0.02,0.3,pi/3,pi/2,2.99 agreed with gamma+sin gamma (worst abs <1.4e-12). The entire proof is analytic; finite samples merely corroborate it. The known k=2 perpendicular case exactly reproduces Finch V=8/3 and S=2(2+pi).

originality.rationale: The exact Finch 2012 orthogonal two-disk metrics are previously known and excluded from novelty. Fresh Resultary searches (four independent semantic queries) retrieved the identical submitted record, a separate orthogonal three-disk result (coordinate planes have no common diameter line), and a displaced-disk mean-width result; none yields the all-k common-diameter volume/surface relation. Read the mathematical statements in both relevant Resultary papers. Finch arXiv:1211.4514 treats three two-disk arrangements, of which only the concentric right-angle case belongs to this family; Bäsel arXiv:1604.07245 treats the displaced-center oloid; Nash–Pir–Sottile–Ying arXiv:1612.09382 classify face lattices and algebraic edge surfaces of pairs, not the metric all-k identity. CHoCC 2020 treats cospherical circles bounding disjoint spherical caps, whereas the present input consists of great circles meeting in the same two antipodal axis points; its published abstract and poster are therefore not directly covering. Its full paper remained inaccessible after legal OA/arXiv searches and an authorized institutional attempt, recorded as a residual risk, not automatic failure. No stronger covering or exact tabulated all-k expression was found; search silence is not proof of priority. The audited parameterized identity and rigid equal-gap maximizers are not logical consequences of the checked special-case formulas.
residual_risks: CHoCC (2020) full paper was not accessible after arXiv/OA searches and authorized Oxford attempt (vpn_disconnected); accessible abstract has incompatible disjoint spherical-cap hypothesis, but hidden generalization cannot be excluded from full text.
A classical formula for convex hulls of many great circles or an equivalent spherical suspension/ruled-surface construction may appear under different terminology in unindexed geometry texts.
Finch 2012 two-disk right-angle V=8/3 and S=2(2+pi) are unambiguously previously known; the new contribution must not count that special case as independent novelty.
No search result alone proves historical uniqueness or excludes unpublished work.

value.rationale: The object is the natural finite k common-diameter generalization of the classical two-perpendicular-disk convex hull. The result identifies a configuration-independent affine relation between two intrinsic Euclidean measures even as the individual measures vary continuously with the angular data, and gives a complete sharp equal-spacing maximizer with equality characterization and controlled degenerate/large-k endpoints. Exact simultaneous surface and volume evaluation is not a routine restatement of the two-disk numerical constants; the central structural step is the global homothetic-section description and uniform patch integral, followed by an all-k strict optimization. A future researcher studying metric geometry of multi-circle hulls can reuse the closed formulas and extremal construction as an exact benchmark. Scope is deliberately restricted to R>0, k>=2 distinct planes, common center and line; no displaced/unequal-radius or arbitrary convex-body result is asserted. The proof is elementary in tools but the complete natural-family invariant and rigid extremizers are mathematically motivated, not arbitrary parameter slices.

limitations: The theorem assumes equal radii, common center, a common diameter line, k>=2 distinct supporting planes; it does not cover one degenerate disk, skew/off-center circles or arbitrary convex bodies.
The all-k identity is proven analytically; finite convex-hull sampling/quadrature is not proof of universal geometric claims.

CHoCC 2020 full text was inaccessible: authorized Oxford attempt returned vpn_disconnected after no arXiv/OA full text was found; abstract suggests nonapplicable disjoint-cap hypothesis but unread theorems remain a bounded originality risk.
The public-facing SLOGAN wording could mislead about the k=1 degenerate case and requires precision review before publication.
Public metadata/review material retains internal operational provenance; publication cannot be attested confidentiality-safe without complete guarded sanitization.
